title: Parkinson's Disease: Medication Timing and Complication Review

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with established Parkinson's disease: exact medicine timing, motor/non-motor complications, swallowing, falls and urgent dopaminergic continuity.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national Parkinson's disease guideline was identified in the sources opened on 14 October 2026. NICE guidance is an international comparator pending Saudi/local adaptation.
SFDA product registration was not verified; any medicine selection requires the current Saudi Drug Information register and hospital formulary.
Exact medicine doses and adjustment sequences remain the movement-disorders specialist's plan.

pathophysiology.summary: Dopamine replacement improves motor function but response fluctuates as disease progresses. Delayed or omitted doses can cause severe immobility and potentially dangerous deterioration. Dopaminergic treatment can cause dyskinesia, hallucinations, sleepiness and impulse-control disorders. Swallowing, autonomic and cognitive complications increase falls and aspiration risk.
keyMechanisms: Dopamine replacement improves motor function but response fluctuates as disease progresses.
Delayed or omitted doses can cause severe immobility and potentially dangerous deterioration.
Dopaminergic treatment can cause dyskinesia, hallucinations, sleepiness and impulse-control disorders.
Swallowing, autonomic and cognitive complications increase falls and aspiration risk.

references.title: NICE NG71: Parkinson's disease in adults

symptoms: Wearing-off, freezing, dyskinesia, falls, hallucinations, sleepiness, constipation, urinary symptoms, swallowing difficulty or impulsive behaviour.
physicalSigns: On/off variation, postural instability, orthostatic hypotension, dyskinesia, cognitive change or aspiration signs.
redFlags: Abrupt severe immobility after missed medicine, fever/rigidity, aspiration, recurrent syncope, acute psychosis or dangerous impulse-control behaviour needs urgent assessment.
precipitants: Late/omitted doses, infection, dehydration, constipation, interacting antiemetics/antipsychotics and reduced absorption.

differentials.condition: Delirium from infection or medicine toxicity
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Acute fluctuating attention and systemic trigger rather than gradual Parkinson progression.

clinicalManagement.title: Protect exact medicine timing
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At every transfer, admission and review
actions: Reconcile the exact preparation, dose and clock time with the patient/carer and Parkinson record.
Do not stop abruptly; if oral delivery is unsafe, obtain urgent movement-disorders and pharmacy advice for an alternative route/formulation.

clinicalManagement.title: Screen motor and non-motor complications
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At each review and after any deterioration
actions: Review wearing-off, dyskinesia, falls, sleepiness, hallucinations, cognition, impulse-control symptoms, blood pressure, constipation and swallowing.
Check for infection, dehydration, interacting medicines and delayed doses before attributing deterioration to progression.

clinicalManagement.title: Adjust through specialist shared decision
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Promptly when complications impair safety or function
actions: Movement-disorders specialists individualise dopaminergic and adjunct treatment.
Refer to physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-and-language therapy and dietetics according to functional findings.

medicationPlan.note: Continue the individual's exact specialist-prescribed regimen at exact times. This topic intentionally does not reproduce doses because regimens are patient-specific; use the medication record, movement-disorders plan, current SFDA/product information and formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Administer at the person's individually prescribed times; do not substitute standard drug-round times.

teaching.scope: Adults with established Parkinson's disease: exact medicine timing, motor/non-motor complications, swallowing, falls and urgent dopaminergic continuity.
pitfalls: Moving doses to routine drug-round times.
Using dopamine-blocking medicines without specialist review.
keyPoints: New deterioration often has a reversible trigger.

patientEducation: Give the patient/carer a current timed medicine list and emergency contact route.
lifestyleAndDiet: Support falls prevention, exercise, constipation plan and safe driving/occupation review.
mdtReferrals: Movement-disorders neurology, Parkinson nurse, pharmacy, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-and-language therapy and dietetics.
dischargeCriteria: Exact dose times reconciled, swallowing safe or alternative plan active, reversible triggers addressed and follow-up booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Specialist review after any regimen change, admission, fall, hallucination, impulse-control concern or swallowing deterioration.
